You didn't ignore the deadline. You couldn't see it. CAPTION You didn't ignore the deadline. You couldn't see it. You had the same two weeks as everyone else. You just found out it was due the moment it turned into tomorrow. ADHD brains often sort time into two boxes: now and not now. Anything in "not now" feels like it doesn't exist yet. It's called time blindness, and it's why the panic always arrives on the last day. So drag the deadline into "now". Put the due date somewhere you look every day, like your lock screen, and give today one small piece of it. Ten minutes counts. Same deadline. Seen sooner.

The fast start isn't the win. Finishing is. You've done this before: two weeks of going all in, every night, every weekend. Then one bad week and you can't even look at it. Obsession feels like progress because it's loud. But it runs on adrenaline, and adrenaline runs out. Discipline is quieter. It just shows up again tomorrow at the same pace. So pick a pace you could keep on your worst day, not your best one. Twenty minutes. One page. One rep. Then stop, even if you want more. Same stairs. One step at a time.

You don't need help. You need company. Same 10 tasks. Alone, you pick up your phone after the first one. Then someone sits down next to you, doesn't say a word, doesn't touch your work, and suddenly you can't stop. That's called body doubling. An ADHD brain often struggles to start on its own, and another person in the room quietly gives it the push it's missing. It's why you clean faster when a friend is over and work better in a café. Try it today: ask someone to sit with you for 25 minutes, in person or on a video call. They do their thing, you do yours. Same tasks. Not alone.

Your to-do list isn't too big. You're just seeing all of it at once. You had the same eight tasks as everyone else. You just spent the whole morning staring at the pile while it got heavier. Many ADHD brains take in a task list as one huge block instead of separate steps. The longer you look at it, the bigger it feels, so you freeze. That's not laziness. It's overwhelm. So stop looking at the pile. Pick the smallest thing on it, something you can finish in two minutes, like replying to one email, and do only that. The pile starts shrinking the second your hands are busy. Same pile. One at a time. ADHD or regular? Tell me which one you are 👇
